discretionaryPoints.perSkillLimitMeaning: The 'maxPerSkill' figure limits how many points can be put into any single skill in that level's allocation (30 at level 1, 15 at each later level). It is not an overall cap on a skill's percentage.
discretionaryPoints.dataModelHint: Store points assigned per skill per level (pointsByLevel[level][skillId]) so the app can enforce each level's limits and show points remaining.
assumptions: For a multi-class thief, points are awarded per thief level, e.g. Fighter 5 / Thief 4 has 60 + 30 x 3 = 150 points, the same as a single-class level 4 thief. Applies to every multi-class combination that includes a thief (confirmed by owner).
Bard discretionary points are separate: see bardDiscretionaryPoints.

slots.source: PHB Table 34: Proficiency Slots (image supplied by owner)
slots.classToSlotGroup: Use classGroups in rules-core.json: fighter/paladin/ranger -> warrior, cleric/druid -> priest, wizard -> wizard, thief/bard -> rogue. Monk: priest (Monk_v1.docx).

levelsPerExtraSlotMeaning.assumed: A character gains one extra slot each time his level reaches a multiple of the table's '#Levels' figure (so a Warrior gains a weapon slot at levels 3, 6, 9...). Confirm from the PHB text.

multiClass.slotsFromOneClassOnly: A multi-class character gains non-weapon proficiency slots from ONE class only, never combined across classes.
multiClass.precedenceNote: Owner wording: Warriors, Cleric, Wizard, then Rogue. Stored by class group (warrior = fighter/paladin/ranger, priest = cleric/druid, wizard = wizard/illusionist, rogue = thief/bard). The class group highest in this list among the character's classes supplies the slots.
multiClass.freeGroups: The character can take proficiencies from every group that any of his classes has access to at the normal slot cost: General plus the own group of each of his classes. Any other group costs +1 slot (crossGroupCost).
multiClass.example: Fighter/Thief: slots come from the Fighter (warrior group). Normal cost for General, Warrior and Rogue proficiencies; every other group costs +1 slot.
multiClass.engineRule: slotClass = the character's class whose group is first in 'precedence'; slots = that class's slots at that class's level (confirmed). cost = slots + (0 if proficiency.groups intersects ['general'] + groupOf(each class) else 1).
multiClass.slotLevel: Slots are counted at the level of the class that supplies them (confirmed by owner), e.g. Fighter 5 / Thief 4 uses fighter level 5.

weaponSlots.rule: Weapon proficiency slots follow the same rules as non-weapon slots: they come from ONE class only, never combined, counted at that class's level. Only the precedence differs.
weaponSlots.precedenceNote: Owner wording: Warrior, Rogue, Priest, Wizard. By class group (warrior = fighter/paladin/ranger, rogue = thief/bard, priest = cleric/druid, wizard = wizard/illusionist). The class group highest in this list supplies the weapon slots.
weaponSlots.example: Fighter/Thief: weapon slots come from the Fighter, at fighter level.
weaponSlots.engineRule: weaponSlotClass = the character's class whose group is first in precedence; slots = that class's weapon slots at that class's level.

nonProficientPenalty.rule: A multi-class character uses the most favourable (smallest) non-proficient weapon penalty among his classes, which follows the same order: Warrior (-2), Rogue (-3), Priest (-3), Wizard (-5).
nonProficientPenalty.example: Fighter/Wizard uses the warrior penalty of -2; Thief/Wizard uses the rogue penalty of -3.

slotCost.source: PHB 'Cost of Weapon Specialization' text (supplied by owner; pasted text ended part-way through the Rath example)
slotCost.rule: Specialising uses extra weapon proficiency slots on the chosen weapon. The first slot makes the character proficient; each further slot is spent on specialisation.
slotCost.example: Rath the dwarf specialising in the warhammer spends two of his four starting slots on it, leaving two to become proficient with other weapons.
assumptions: Thrown and other missile weapons (not stated in the pasted text) are not yet assigned a cost.
Where weapon specialisation applies by class is governed by eligibleClasses (single-class Fighter).

relatedWeaponRule.rule: When a character uses a weapon similar to one he is proficient with, his attack penalty is one-half the normal non-proficient amount, rounded up.
relatedWeaponRule.examples: Warrior -1 instead of -2; wizard -3 instead of -5; priest -2 instead of -3; rogue -2 instead of -3.
relatedWeaponRule.monk: The Monk uses the priest group: -3 non-proficient, -2 related.
relatedWeaponRule.dmDecision: The PHB leaves the exact related weapons to the DM; these are its "likely categories".

Footman's mace, horseman's mace, morning star, flail, hammer, club

mappingAssumptions: "hammer" = melee warhammer and Warhammer (Thrown) (id warhammerThrown, a gear.json missileRanges row)
"composite bow" = composite short bow and composite long bow
Hand crossbow is not in the crossbow group (PHB lists heavy and light only)
Each weapon appears in at most one group, so a weapon is related only to the others in its own group
relatedWeaponGroups.engineHint: If the weapon used is not proficient but another weapon in the same group is, apply the related penalty instead of the full penalty.

crossGroupCost.rule: A proficiency from a group other than the class's own group costs one extra slot.
crossGroupCost.ownGroup: The class group from rules-core classGroups. For every class this matches the first group printed on Table 38.
assumptions: General proficiencies never cost the extra slot, for any class (to be confirmed).
A proficiency listed in several groups costs the normal slots if ANY of its groups is the class's own group (or General), otherwise one extra slot.
For multi-class characters a proficiency costs the normal slots if it belongs to General or to the own group of ANY of the character's classes; otherwise +1 slot (confirmed by owner, see multiClass).
